claims.statement: TermindPersistence.makeContainer is the single SwiftData container factory: it fixes the current V40 schema and migration plan, disables automatic SwiftData CloudKit storage, rejects an in-memory request with a file URL, and propagates store-open errors.

The macOS and mobile composition roots retain one process-level ModelContainer and inject contexts into persistence-backed services; the mobile root creates Application Support before opening its file store and uses in-memory dependencies for test/injected operation.

`SwiftDataHostRepository` projects SwiftData rows into revisioned host-library snapshots and commits host changes atomically with a repository revision and Vault mutation recording; it rolls the context back on failure and publishes change streams only after saving.

Host deletion is represented as a durable saga: the request transaction writes a pending-deletion marker and outbox jobs, snapshots hide pending hosts, later work clears dependent data, and finalization removes host-owned identities, the host, and marker.

Frozen schema endpoints remain registered through V40: V35 adds native History journals and capability state, V36 removes the retired importer table, V37 adds cloud record/replica state, V38 adds deletion handoff and asset cleanup, V39 adds assistant model selection, and V40 drops retired per-category quarantine models; these recent stages are lightweight and preserve the custom V31→V34 history device backfill.

Persistence compatibility tests open legacy V1/V14 and fixed historical V28 fixtures, verify reopen and full-schema independent in-memory behavior, and retain V27/V30/V31 plus V35-to-current coverage. V28 migration and reopening preserve host settings, charset, identity/key references, ordered environment variables, snippets, Known Hosts and connection history, with the existing installation ID used for device backfill.

Durable credentials are represented by non-secret references and storage metadata; `SecretStoring` resolves those references from a concrete secret store and converts them to runtime SSH secret/key credential values, while the app roots use Keychain in live composition and in-memory storage for tests.

`AISecretStore` keeps only reference/location/deletion metadata in SwiftData and secret bytes in Keychain; it gates new iCloud placement on authorization and both sync switches, verifies the cloud write before removing the device copy, and keeps deletion markers to prevent a delayed Keychain value from being read again.

`SSHSecret` is one-shot wipeable runtime storage: it clears the source buffer, shares one owned allocation across copies, consumes it at most once, and overwrites/deallocates it before return; connection configurations can clear credentials, proxy secrets, and jump secrets while retaining non-secret provenance.

When interaction is forbidden, SSH connection requests replace passphrase- or user-presence-protected credentials with `interactionRequired` and make host-key or keyboard-interactive prompts fail, preventing silent auxiliary connections from consuming interactive secrets.

`GRDBMemoryStore` is a lazily opened actor-owned SQLite store in its own directory: first access creates the directory, enables WAL, migrates tables/FTS/triggers including the policy-learning migration, and later `close` or `destroy` releases the queue and optionally removes that directory.

Hermes memory applies review operations only when the supplied expected state matches the current state, and its history replacement stores redacted user/assistant/tool messages, removes absent sessions, and supports FTS-backed or short-query fallback search.

Agent run persistence writes durable snapshots and sanitized message/tool data, marks unfinished runs interrupted at repository initialization, and reconstructs recorded tool results that were committed before their transcript row after a process interruption.

Quarantine fences writes by container/environment/account/zone/owner/consumer, retaining JSON payloads or native CKRecord archives and system fields; the retired History cross-zone importer no longer supplies a target fence.

Recovery checkpoints require fresh fetches for new or interrupted replica scopes while preserving journal intent, and clearing a restriction occurs in the same persistence commit as supported remote reconciliation; disk-reopen and rollback tests cover these contracts.

HistorySyncStore commits events and terminal tombstones atomically, retaining 250 events deterministically. Device names journal independently and survive History clearing. Host cleanup journals History deletion, ordinary edits only journal Vault.

Assistant restore and truncation share canonical run start/UUID and message run/sequence/time/role/UUID order. Truncation validates before mutation, removes the target message and suffix plus later runs, and preserves a same-run prefix with a neutral completed summary ending at its last retained non-tool message.

Partial-run graph cleanup prioritizes source-message then call ownership before an inclusive unknown-ownership timestamp fallback that also covers modern provider-native events preceding their source-message snapshot, deletes associated result/review and message backing rows, and prunes only compactions with removed explicit boundaries. Restore infers legacy sources and recovered result ownership before compaction projection.

An edited replacement is stored in a same-ID completed staging run ordered after all retained runs; its first real snapshot transactionally adopts only that message's run/sequence, retains replay/attachment backing, deletes staging and preserves ordinary historical owners. Failed/interrupted snapshots share the adoption path, and subsequent saves retain the adopted chronological lower bound.

Edited target, removed later and adopted staging runs are retired within the repository instance; late snapshots/events are ignored. Truncation and snapshot save roll back SwiftData and restore the prior in-memory retired-ID set on errors, without adding persisted tombstones.

Assistant history edits publish after truncation commits; captured missing-model/credential failure and preparation interruption also save a terminal snapshot before live adoption, with save failure leaving adoption unprojected. Queued-before-start runtime cancellation is distinct: it projects cancellation when launching a best-effort save, so stop-and-wait does not guarantee a successful durable snapshot.

Desktop host deletion requests the durable deletion before clearing command, SFTP and connection History and projecting the host out; mobile performs live-workspace, assistant, transfer and forwarding cleanup before requesting deletion and leaves its three History clears to the registered outbox handler, which can resume after startup.

Desktop SwiftData composition shares the container main context among many persistence services and terminates on database-open failure; mobile composition creates separate contexts for several services, shares a vault context among host and history/device repositories, and throws on container-open failure rather than replacing the store.

MemoryIndexedAgentRepository keeps SwiftData-backed agent conversations authoritative and schedules the separate GRDB history index only after successful terminal saves, creation, title changes, truncation, or deletion; MemoryModel loads that history through AgentRunPersisting when enabled and unsuspended, coalesces index requests, and waits for indexing before search.
GRDB memory history replacement compares redacted message IDs and content rather than timestamps alone, so edited turns with retained timestamps still refresh the derived searchable index.

Memory suspension invalidates generation-bound session contexts and access, cancels indexing and reviews, and stops new work without deleting storage; mobile invokes it on background and resumes on active scene, while desktop invokes it during termination.

After a memory write commits across a suspension, its old-generation caller is cancelled instead of publishing stale state and the active generation reloads the committed value; on resume the model schedules history indexing and stale pre-suspension reviews cannot apply.

Disabling Hermes memory closes its GRDB store without deletion; destroy disables access, joins cancelled work, removes the dedicated directory, and records a pending-destroy preference that prevents reenable and retries cleanup on next startup after a failure; surviving agent history can be indexed again after successful destroy.

The V28 fixture generator records historical source commit 0dc173d4b1d190071d35bc66f80ebb767d8b950c and its expected schema checksum and requires generating against that historical Persistence framework; the frozen V28 Host and registered endpoint preserve compatibility without changing the current V40 container API or replacing stores after an opening failure.
MobileAppTests constructs MobileAppModel from the migrated V28 disk container twice and checks the app's host library, identity reference and connection history to cover startup and relaunch.

macOS `TermindApp` opens the shared factory during initialization with a default file-backed store for normal launches, but DEBUG XCTest and screenshot demos use an in-memory container; screenshot demos return before live persistence wiring, and the retained container is injected into both main and external-authentication window scenes.

The fixed V28 compatibility fixture is generated from the historical Persistence framework at 0dc173d4b1d190071d35bc66f80ebb767d8b950c, with a recorded expected checksum and synthetic credential references rather than stored secret bytes; it includes a host, identity/key reference, group, snippet, known host, event and existing installation ID.

The V28-to-V30 Host replacement keeps historical `port`, `identityID`, and `charset` column names for SSH while defaulting new Telnet fields; V30 replaces the historical Known Host shape to remove its obsolete mismatch flag, and V31-to-V34 migration assigns existing connection events the stored installation ID and creates an independent device record.

The V28 fixture compatibility test copies a historical store to disk and opens the same path twice through the production container factory; on each open it checks projected Host/Identity/key and ordered environment settings, snippet and known host, connection history with original installation ID/device backfill, and default workspace preferences, rather than only checking current in-memory schema declarations.

The V36 migration drops only the retired History importer checkpoint; native device rows, envelopes and account bindings survive reopening a V35 disk store, while V31/V34 Vault History tombstones and binding are not imported into the new History journal.
Local SwiftData schema migrations are independent of cloud envelope format versions; advancing the current schema to V40 does not itself advance the versioned cloud wire codecs.

Scoped record and replica state persists cloud presence and physical-deletion acknowledgements across cursor resets; a V38 deletion handoff records the causal version so inventory reconciliation preserves a newer explicit recreation rather than treating the old delete as a deletion of the new value.
V38 asset cleanup work remains durable until the category-owned cache directory has been removed successfully, allowing purge completion to retry after interrupted filesystem work.
V39 persists per-conversation assistant model selection as provider and model IDs in SwiftData; both platform roots inject the selection repository separately from Keychain-backed credential storage.

V40 drops retired unscoped Vault, AI-configuration and Metrics quarantine tables while retaining scoped quarantine and record-presence state; V30 and V39 disk migration tests check that old category rows are not imported as scoped restrictions.

Hermes GRDB migration `hermes-policy-learning-v2` drops the obsolete snapshots table and persists deduplicated learning events and reviewed-correction checkpoints, separately from SwiftData schema and CloudKit wire migrations.

GRDB review and correction writes compare the supplied expected memory state with the current state before committing; review also marks specified learning events reviewed in the same transaction, leaving later events unreviewed.
